The operational process described for Fashion Forward relies on an outdated first-in-first-out (FIFO) storage system. The primary bottleneck identified is the physical arrangement of inventory, where newer stock is placed behind older items. This configuration creates a significant efficiency issue: accessing newer inventory requires time-consuming reorganization efforts to move older stock aside. This inefficiency slows down the shipment process and increases labor costs associated with manual reorganization.

To improve efficiency, Fashion Forward should consider implementing a more dynamic storage system, such as a first-expired-first-out (FEFO) system if applicable, or a slotting optimization strategy that places high-turnover or newer items in more accessible locations. Additionally, adopting a warehouse management system (WMS) with real-time inventory tracking could help optimize pick paths and reduce the need for manual reorganization.
